{{Short description|Human cognitive faculty}}
{{Platonism}}
In [[Platonism]], '''''dianoia''''' ([[Ancient Greek|Greek]]: [[:Wiktionary:διάνοια|διάνοια]]) is the human [[cognition|cognitive]] faculty associated with the BC portion of the [[analogy of the divided line]] and related to ''[[discursive reasoning|discursive]]'' thinking about mathematical and technical subjects.{{sfn|Boyle|1973|p=2}} It stands in contrast to the immediate, cognitive process of ''[[intuition|intuitive]]'' apprehension or ''[[ Noesis (Platonism)|noesis]]''.{{sfnp|Hendrix|2015|p=114}}

In Aristotle, ''dianoia'' is subdivided into theoretical knowledge ''([[Techne|technē]])'' and practical knowledge ''([[Phronesis|phronēsis]])''.{{sfnp|Blackburn|2016}}
